question.problem: It takes $20$ minutes for a slug to crawl $90$ centimeters at a constant pace. How much time does it take for the slug to crawl $450$ centimeters?
question.worked_solution:
Speed is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*:

$$
\text{speed}=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

To find the speed, in centimeters per minute, we divide the number of centimeters, which is $90,$ by the number of minutes, $20.$ This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{90}{20} & =\frac{90÷10}{20÷10} \\  & =\frac{9}{2} \\  & =9÷2 \\  & =4.5.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the speed of the slug is $4.5$ centimeters per minute. 

To find the time it took the slug to cover $450$ centimeters, we divide the distance by $4.5.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{time} & =\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}} \\  & =\frac{450}{4.5} \\  & =\frac{450\cdot 10}{4.5\cdot 10} \\  & =\frac{4\,500}{45} \\  & =\frac{45\cdot 100}{45} \\  & =100.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, it takes the slug $100$ minutes to crawl $450$ centimeters.
